findings: ETT.tex:1301–1306: under the repair of DEC-148, (iii)⇒(i) needs no quasi-limit of curves (O'Neill Def. 7, Prop. 8, Thm 35). A chain argument with no limit curve and no time function proves it when M is also causally open in the past and future (J^∓ of open sets open) and J^±(S) is closed. Those two hypotheses are what the proof uses beyond the printed list. Both hold in the model spaces and under SingularFlatAxioms. Proofs: Causal.Causality.globallyHyperbolic_of_isCauchySurface_of_isOpen and geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen, sorry-free.

DEC-148's local causal closedness is necessary, not only sufficient. Chronological Minkowski space ℝ^{1,n} (n ≥ 1) satisfies every other hypothesis of the engine and of the sorry-free repaired form, and is not globally hyperbolic (Causal.chronoMinkowski_engine_hypotheses, chronoMinkowski_not_locallyCausallyClosed). So the counterexample of OQ-32 is exactly the failure of local causal closedness.

OQ-32's second question (does J⁻(q) ∩ J⁺(S) stay compact under the repair?): yes when J^∓ of open sets are open and J^±(S) closed. It lies in a compact set (exists_isCompact_Jminus_inter_Jplus) and J^±(p) are closed (isClosed_Jplus_singleton_of_isCauchySurface). Under DEC-148 alone it is open, like the theorem.

ETT.tex:255 (def:category_topological_spacetimes) makes every topological spacetime second countable. theo:geroch's proof needs it, through inextensible curves (exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable); the earlier formalization of theo:geroch had dropped it.
questions: Reading of DEC-148 '≤ closed near every point'. Taken: every point has ONE open neighbourhood U with ≤_U closed in U × U, the weakest form considered (a closed ≤_M gives it with U = M). Alternatives: a basis of such U (O'Neill's convex neighbourhoods); or ≤_M closed near the diagonal. With strong causality and causal arc-connectedness the reading taken yields ≤_M closed on arbitrarily small compact neighbourhoods (LocallyCausallyClosed.exists_isCompact), which is all the proof uses.

Should theo:geroch also carry causal openness (DEC-8 two-sided; or only J^∓ of open sets open) and chronal cones I^±(x) ≠ ∅ (or J^±(S) closed for Cauchy surfaces)? With them the repaired equivalence is sorry-free (geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed_of_causallyOpen). Without them its truth is open. No reading taken: the principal repaired form (geroch_of_locallyCausallyClosed) follows DEC-148 alone and keeps the sorry.

kb_proposals: Local causal closedness (DEC-148) is Causality.LocallyCausallyClosed (CausalScaffold.GerochEquiv): one open U ∋ p with ≤_U closed in U × U. A closed ≤ or (i) on a tarentin T2 space gives it. With strong causality and causal arc-connectedness it closes ≤_M on small compact neighbourhoods (LocallyCausallyClosed.exists_isCompact). Test against chronoMinkowski, which fails it.

(iii)⇒(i) without limit curves or a time function: Causality.globallyHyperbolic_of_isCauchySurface_of_isOpen. The hypotheses are second countable, locally compact, metrizable, cac, SC, locally causally closed, J^∓ of open sets open, and J^±(S) closed. Proof: a chain without limit from a local step (exists_antitone_chain), concatenated into one curve (exists_causalCurveIn_univ_of_chain) that lies under an inextensible curve (exists_inextensible_above_chain).

A sequence with no limit from a local frontier step: take closed balls of a compatible metric (letI := metrizableSpaceMetric M) of half the supremal admissible radius. frontier_closedBall_subset_sphere then makes each step long, so a limit is impossible (Causality.exists_antitone_chain, pure topology).

theo:geroch_sing's equivalence is sorry-free for SingularFlatAxioms + StronglyCausal + LocallyCausallyClosed (CausalScaffold.GerochIIIImpI). At E≥0-manifolds the only input left is LocallyCausallyClosed from the models' closed relations, a layer-3 lemma.

Typechecking a new scaffold module against a rewritten scaffold module (refines kb/0034): compile the rewritten one to /tmp/X with `lake env lean -R scaffold -o`. Then symlink every other CausalScaffold olean the new module imports into /tmp/X/CausalScaffold: Lean takes the CausalScaffold root from the first LEAN_PATH entry that has it.

In term-mode `let ⟨…⟩ := e; …` patterns write `_`, not `-`; and a multi-line `fun p => let ⟨…⟩ := …` with the body on the next line does not parse: use `fun p => by obtain …; exact …`. Give map_mem_closure its function explicitly (f := fun w => (w, y)).
